title: Maximum of Every Window

concept.title: A deque that keeps only the candidates for the maximum
body: For every window of `k` consecutive elements you want its **maximum**. Looking at all `k` elements of each window costs `n * k`. A **deque** (double-ended queue: you can add and remove at **both** ends) does it in O(n).

Keep in the deque the **indexes** of the elements that can still become the maximum of a window, in order of position, with **decreasing values** from the front to the back. When a new element `a[i]` arrives, **remove from the back** every element that is not larger than it: they are older and smaller, so they can never be the maximum again. Then add `i` at the back. Also **remove from the front** an index that has left the window (`i - k`). The front is always the maximum of the current window.
This structure is called a **monotonic queue**. Every index enters and leaves once, so the work is O(n).

statement: Given an array of `n` integers and a window size `k`, print the maximum of every window of `k` consecutive elements (there are `n - k + 1` windows), from the left to the right.
outputFormat: Print `n - k + 1` numbers separated by spaces.
hints: Keep a deque of indexes whose values decrease from the front to the back.
Before adding a new index, remove the indexes at the back whose values are not larger.
Remove the front index when it is no longer inside the window; the front is the maximum.

explanation: The deque holds the indexes of the possible maximums with decreasing values. Smaller older elements are removed at the back, expired indexes at the front, and the front is the maximum of the window.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

from collections import deque
dq = deque()
out = []
for i in range(n):
    while dq and a[dq[-1]] <= a[i]:
        dq.pop()
    dq.append(i)
    if dq[0] <= i - k:
        dq.popleft()
    if i >= k - 1:
        out.append(a[dq[0]])
print(*out)
